requirements.statement: Package managers must be able to award a supplier package to one supplier.
requirements.source_quote: Package managers must be able to award a supplier package to one supplier.
ambiguity_notes: Which suppliers can be chosen (for example only those who bid or were invited) is not stated.
Whether an award can be undone or changed is not stated.
Whether all package managers or only some (for example the package's own manager) may award is not stated.
Which users the read-only state applies to (package managers, suppliers, administrators) is not stated.
Which parts of the package are locked is not stated.
Whether there is any exception or way to reopen an awarded package is not stated.

requirements.statement: Suppliers must be notified when they win.
requirements.source_quote: Suppliers must be notified when they win.
ambiguity_notes: The notification channel (email, in-app, other) is not stated.
The notification content is not stated.
'When they win' is not defined as a moment: at the time of award or at some later step.

assumptions.text: 'Suppliers' who 'win' in the third statement means the single supplier to whom a package is awarded under the first statement.
assumptions.why: The text does not link the two statements explicitly, and 'win' is not defined.
assumptions.impact: Determines who receives the notification and the event that triggers it.
assumptions.to_confirm: Confirm that winning means being the supplier selected in the award action, and that only that supplier is notified.

clarifying_questions.question: Which suppliers can a package be awarded to, for example only suppliers who submitted a bid or were invited?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: Defines the data and the eligibility rules behind the award action.
clarifying_questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Any supplier might be selectable, including ones who never took part.

clarifying_questions.question: Can an award be undone or changed after it is made, and if so by whom?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: The award is possibly irreversible and interacts with the read-only rule.
clarifying_questions.consequence_if_unanswered: A wrong award could not be corrected, or reversal might be built without a rule for it.

clarifying_questions.question: Which package managers may award a package: any of them, or only the manager responsible for that package?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: Sets permissions for a significant action.
clarifying_questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Permissions cannot be specified and an unauthorised user might award a package.

clarifying_questions.question: Who is the read-only state for, and which parts of an awarded package does it lock?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: Decides what editing is blocked and for which roles.
clarifying_questions.consequence_if_unanswered: Behaviour of awarded packages cannot be specified, and the scope may be too wide or too narrow.

clarifying_questions.question: How should the winning supplier be notified (email, in-app, other) and what should the notification say?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: Determines integration, content and any contact data needed.
clarifying_questions.consequence_if_unanswered: The channel and content would have to be guessed.

clarifying_questions.question: At what moment is the supplier notified, immediately when the award is made or at a later step, and should other suppliers be told anything?
clarifying_questions.why_it_matters: Sets the trigger for the notification and its audience.
clarifying_questions.consequence_if_unanswered: The trigger may fire too early, for example before a reversible award is final.

proposed_status_changes.reason: Who the read-only state applies to and what it covers is not stated.
Notification channel, content and trigger are not stated.
